phi_check.method: For each of the 23 RET-Nxx equations, searched registry/CANONICAL.json (967 entries) by keyword (agent/network/consensus/tunnel/hallucination/reflection/recursive/provenance/freeze/frozen/world-closure/session-reset terms drawn from each RET equation's own name and symbols) for a structurally-equivalent object under the Equivalence Registry phi-criterion (documented bijective renaming / fixed positive scale / fixed constant substitution, exact, on a shared domain -- no limits, no approximations; per docs/EQ_CODE_SCHEME.md).

candidates_reviewed_and_ruled_out.candidate: EQ-015/H.12.v1 (CAN-067, 'gain-side/tunnel-side directional functions', G_s=g(...); T_s=h(...); Delta_s=G_s-T_s; tunnel iff Delta_s<0)
candidates_reviewed_and_ruled_out.result: NOT phi-equivalent. CAN-067's 'tunnel' is an unrelated pre-existing Toledo term: a scalar gain-vs-loss directional-function difference in a Human-Return CTSA6 context, with no agents, no network, no recursion, no reciprocal-lineage/effective-alternative/resistance components. No bijective renaming/scaling maps CAN-067's (G_s,T_s,Delta_s) onto RET-N11's network-regime definition. Flagged in RET-N11's drift_note so the two 'tunnel' usages in the library are not conflated.

candidates_reviewed_and_ruled_out.checked_against: RET-N13 (multi-model consensus readout) and RET-N14 (consensus does not entail validation)
candidates_reviewed_and_ruled_out.result: NOT phi-equivalent to either, but structurally cognate to RET-N14 (same 'MultiConsensus =/=> X' non-entailment shape). The consequent (GeographicCompleteness, an ARAYA-lineage dataset-coverage property) is not a renaming/scaling of RET-N14's consequent (Validation(c), an epistemic-status property) -- different theories under the same form. Recorded as a same_form_different_theory relation on RET-N14 rather than merged or used as a parent.

candidates_reviewed_and_ruled_out.candidate: EQ-015/P.19.v1 (RUS-0027, Perron-Frobenius / doubly-stochastic-matrix opinion consensus, tier untagged)
candidates_reviewed_and_ruled_out.result: NOT phi-equivalent. RUS-0027 is a convergence theorem over an iterated doubly-stochastic matrix P (spectral-radius argument); RET-N13 is a simple one-shot average of a binary acceptance indicator across k models, with no matrix, no iteration, and no convergence claim. Different mathematical objects; ruled out.

NOT phi-equivalent, but same root (A.8) and same freeze-then-verify shape. CAN-191 freezes new releases pending citation-integrity correction; AOWC freezes a claim/prediction pending AI-off world-side evaluation. Different frozen object, different correction step -- no bijective renaming maps one onto the other. Recorded as a same_form_different_theory relation on RET-N17, and as an additional 'reads' parent (the freeze mechanism itself is read from this A.8 family) rather than a merge.

phi_check.result_summary: No RET-Nxx equation was found phi-equivalent to an existing CANONICAL.json object; all 23 are correctly proposed as new readings/derivations rather than existing Toledo equations, consistent with the manuscript's own labelling. Four near-miss candidates (CAN-067, CAN-246, RUS-0027, CAN-191) were identified by keyword search, individually checked under the exact phi-criterion, and ruled out as distinct objects (two recorded as same_form_different_theory cross-references rather than silently dropped).

rule_6_priority_words.verdict: No rule-6 violation found. Every non-exempt hit is either an ordinal ('first of several', 'first step', 'first token'), a compound lineage/methodology descriptor ('Genesis-first', 'Problem-first' -- naming the programme's own derivation order, not a comparative-superiority claim), a negated/anti-novelty statement, or a property attributed to external claims rather than to this manuscript's own results. rule_17_citation_resolvability.method: Cross-checked every in-text external/self-citation topic against the References list (17 entries) and vice versa.
findings: All 17 References entries resolve to an identifiable in-text discussion: Bara 2026 (sec.37.7, Sybil), Cheng et al. 2026 (sec.37.3, sycophancy), Jamshidi 2026 (sec.37.5, multi-agent hallucination), Kohli 2026 (sec.37.6, correlated LLM judges), Meyer/Miggelbrink/Nguyen 2026 (sec.37.4, named inline), Nguyen 2020 (sec.37.1, named inline), Romeo & Conti 2026 (sec.37.2, automation bias), and the 10 Lahtee/Toledo-programme self-citations (all named as programme anchors in the Manuscript Status section, line 64, or cited by title/topic elsewhere: Toledo v1.3.0 sec.'Mathematical source policy'; Readout Genesis throughout; Readout Universe and GLOSA in 'Cross-domain interpretation policy'; CTSA Human-Return via CAN-076's 'CTSA v9.1'; How Humans Should Converse with AI via the Dialogue Conversion Protocol referenced sec.26/33/48).

Soft finding (not a hard rule-17 failure): sections 37.2, 37.3, 37.5, 37.6, 37.7 introduce their external source as 'Automation-bias research...', 'Recent experimental work shows...', 'Recent multi-agent work models...', 'Work on LLM evaluation panels shows...', 'Recent work formalizes...' -- with no inline author-year marker, unlike sec.37.1 ('Nguyen distinguishes...') and sec.37.4 ('Meyer, Miggelbrink, and Nguyen distinguish...') which do name authors inline. Each of the 5 unattributed sentences has exactly one uniquely-matching, non-orphaned Reference entry (topic correspondence is 1:1 and unambiguous), so every citation IS resolvable -- but resolution currently requires topic-matching rather than an explicit inline marker. Recommend adding '(Author, year)' inline at these 5 points before the chair's registration pass, for a clean hard rule-17 pass rather than a resolvable-by-inference one.
rule_17_citation_resolvability.verdict: Rule 17 satisfied (every citation resolves, none orphaned, no dangling in-text claim without a matching reference) with one hygiene recommendation (add inline author-year markers at 5 points) flagged for the chair.
